text:
The specific mechanism here is government-funded childcare provision — a publicly subsidized early childhood care entitlement (30 hours/week). This is squarely about childcare/early education public expenditure.

Primary: I (Health, Education, and Welfare — specifically I2, education/childcare institutions, or I3 welfare provision for families)

Secondary consideration: H (public expenditure on a publicly provided good — H4/H5), and J (labor supply effects on parents, particularly mothers — J2). The childcare subsidy has a well-known labor supply dimension, but the statement itself names the service provision, not the labor market effect.

{"primary": "I", "secondary": ["H"]}
